content.text: No non-compete, field-of-use, or territory restriction on Clear Capital appears anywhere in the agreement. The only restrictive covenant is a mutual employee non-solicit, and § 4's limit on reselling Contractor's own pre-existing materials is an IP license-scope term, not a restraint on our business.

input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding Clear Capital, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). A full-text scan for "compete/competing", "shall not", "exclusiv", "solicit", "restrict", "field of use" and "territory", plus review of the engagement scope (§ 1), term (§ 1.2) and termination (§ 6), surfaced only two adjacent provisions, neither of which is a covenant not to compete: (i) § 13 (p0047) is a mutual, employee-only non-solicit limited to personnel with direct Services involvement, running for the term plus one year — a restraint on hiring, not on our business lines or products, and it binds RadialSpark equally; and (ii) § 4 (p0020) provides that Company "shall not resell or make use of" Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials and administrative records other than in connection with the software received under the Agreement — a scope-of-license/IP-ownership term protecting Contractor's background IP, not a field-of-use restriction on Clear Capital's own or third-party products. Nothing prevents us from developing competing functionality internally, engaging other vendors, or making acquisitions. No redline required.
